candidates.statement: Additionally, in coordinate space $\ensuremath{\boldsymbol{p}} = -i \nabla$ and acts directly on the wave function (for sub-leading terms involving powers of $\ensuremath{\boldsymbol{p}}$, particular care must be taken when performing the Fourier transform from momentum to coordinate space).

Second, the final states, which play a significant role in the nuclear response functions, may include high-momentum knocked-out nucleons, whose kinetic energies should be calculated relativistically for accurate results.

The nucleon form factors ${F}_1(Q^2)$ and $F_2(Q^2)$ appearing in the covariant expression of the electromagnetic current -- Eq. ([\[eq:relvector\]](#eq:relvector){reference-type="ref" reference="eq:relvector"}) -- must also be treated consistently since they depend on the nucleon momentum through $Q^2$.
In principle, their expansion around the quasielastic peak introduces terms that should be included for consistency.
A similar treatment should be in principle applied to two-body currents.

Focusing on the dominant contributions at large $q$, the prefactor $(2m\tau_{qe})\alpha(q)/q^2$ in the LO high-$q$ expansion should be compared to the factor $1/2m$ appearing in Eq. [\[eq:transverse_NR_LO\]](#eq:transverse_NR_LO){reference-type="eqref" reference="eq:transverse_NR_LO"}.
